servicios.title: Five fronts of intervention, {accent} scientific method.
servicios.subtitle: Each service combines verifiable technical foundations with its own intervention model, designed to turn field data into management decisions.

items.label: Industrial Hygiene
items.title: Industrial Hygiene
items.tagline: A systems model for studying what the eye can't measure.
items.description: We design and implement a hygiene studies systems model that translates the physical conditions of the work environment—sound, light, and temperature—into actionable management information. Instead of a single, isolated measurement, we build full-operation sound maps and lighting maps, backed by sound level surveys, lux surveys, and thermal stress assessments, and cross-reference them with the production process to prioritize where to intervene first.
items.techText: industrial acoustics (Crocker), ergonomics and thermal engineering (Parsons, Incropera), thermal comfort and stress (Fanger), and lighting engineering (Boyce, IES, CIE). Aligned with ISO 7730, ISO 7243, ISO 7933, and ISO 11079.

items.label: Road Safety
items.title: Road Safety
items.tagline: Systemic Road Safety Model: regulatory compliance and behavioral science, in a single framework.
items.description: We work road safety on two complementary levels. The classic PESV (Colombia's statutory road safety plan), which meets the current regulatory framework for owned and contracted fleets. And our own Systemic Road Safety Model, which goes beyond documentary compliance: it measures and models the operation's actual road risk based on driver behavior, the vehicle, and the environment.
items.techText: road risk measurement and modeling (Evans — Traffic Safety), behavioral science and driver performance (Evans — Traffic Safety and the Driver), and an evidence-based systemic understanding of motorcyclist accident rates (The Hurt Report).

items.label: Mechanical and Facility Risk
items.title: Mechanical and Facility Risk
items.tagline: Systemic Intervention Model: continuous improvement applied to operations, tools, and machinery.
items.description: A strategy that guides the intervention of the most significant risks arising from operations, and the use of tools, equipment, and machinery, in production plants, workshops, and operations with critical assets, through a systematic continuous improvement process.
items.techText: defining responsibilities and scope → identifying and prioritizing critical areas, processes, equipment, and activities → technical diagnosis of the conditions causing the risk → designing and implementing measures for people, equipment, and processes → tracking through management indicators → evaluating and continuously improving the strategy.

items.label: Risk-Based Maintenance
items.title: Risk-Based Maintenance
items.tagline: Systemic Maintenance Model: fewer incidents, more reliability.
items.description: We design risk-based maintenance strategies aimed at reducing the operation's accident rate—both what affects people and what compromises property and critical infrastructure. We prioritize investment and technical effort based on the actual probability and consequence of each asset's failure, integrating operational reliability with process safety management.
items.techText: criticality analysis and risk-based inspection (RBI), and reliability-centered maintenance (RCM), adjusted to each plant's operating reality.

items.label: Scientific Modeling of Social Behavior
items.title: Scientific Modeling of Social Behavior
items.tagline: Systemic Behavior Model: fixed environments and variable environments.
items.description: We build a systemic model that interprets human behavior toward risk based on two forces: fixed environments—structure, rules, and organizational culture—and variable environments—the context, pressure, and opportunity of the moment. It's the same framework we use to understand why people expose themselves to risk in operations, one we extend to broader organizational behavior phenomena, such as public and private corruption models: another form of systemic behavior that can also be explained—and addressed—through its fixed and variable environments.
items.techText: complexity science applied to human behavior, integrating organizational, social, and individual variables within a single systemic analysis framework.

metodologia.title: From the static matrix to the {accent} of risk.
metodologia.intro: GTC 45 organizes hazards into independent columns, each with its own action plan. In practice, hazards coexist and interact: evidence on musculoskeletal disorders and on systemic accident models shows that risk emerges from that interaction, not from the sum of isolated parts. That's why we adopt ISO 31000 as our framework and network science as our calculation engine.

shift.fromDesc: A fixed value per hazard, revalued once a year, with seven categories managed in separate columns.
shift.toDesc: Agents and Conditions interact continuously; the risk level is recalculated with the system's actual state.

metodologia.componentsLabel: The model's four components, per ISO 31000

components.title: Agents
components.description: People: capabilities, physiological, cognitive, and psychosocial state, internal and external behavior, social interaction.

components.title: Conditions
components.description: The work environment: technologies, processes, organizational factors, physical infrastructure, and external environment.

components.title: Events
components.description: Emerging node-types by damage mechanism: falls, entrapment, overexertion, chemical exposure, and more.

components.title: Consequences
components.description: Expected severity, calibrated with historical accident data instead of a fixed, subjective table.

metodologia.cycleTitle: A continuous cycle, not an annual exercise.
metodologia.cycleSubtitle: The four stages recognized by GTC 45 and ISO 31000 remain, but they now run on the dynamic network: each with its own update frequency.

stages.label: Identification
stages.title: Identification
stages.tagline: Build and update the network's structure.
stages.description: This defines which nodes exist—agents, conditions, events—and what connections exist between them. It's the lowest-frequency stage: reviewed when processes or technology change, or when new evidence emerges about previously unconsidered interactions.
stages.frequency: low — only when the work system's structure changes.

stages.label: Valuation
stages.title: Valuation
stages.tagline: Calculate the risk level in real time.
stages.description: Probability and consequence of each event-node are combined at a given moment. Unlike GTC 45, this valuation isn't done once a year: it's recalculated continuously as the source nodes' values change—shift by shift or daily.
stages.frequency: continuous — shift by shift or daily.

stages.label: Evaluation
stages.title: Evaluation
stages.description: The calculated risk level is compared against acceptability bands—acceptable, tolerable, not acceptable, unacceptable—to determine which events require priority intervention at a given time.
stages.frequency: punctual — every time the valuation is recalculated.

stages.label: Control
stages.title: Control
stages.tagline: Intervene where sensitivity analysis points to.
stages.description: Interventions are applied specifically to the nodes that, according to the network's sensitivity analysis, contribute most to the assessed risk, and it's verified that the intervention reduced the projected trajectory.
stages.frequency: targeted — when an alert triggers or an improvement cycle closes.

metodologia.toolsTitle: The mathematical tools behind the model.
metodologia.toolsSubtitle: Systems thinking and network science, translated into concrete calculation and diagnostic tools.

rows.name: Network centrality analysis
rows.fn: Identifies the structurally most critical nodes, regardless of the specific value they take at a given moment.
rows.freq: Low — when the network's structure changes

rows.name: State-space model
rows.fn: Projects the evolution of each node's risk level over time and allows simulating the effect of interventions.

rows.name: Dynamic Bayesian Networks
rows.fn: Diagnoses, when an event crosses the critical threshold, which node or combination of nodes contributed the most.

rows.name: Noisy-OR function
rows.fn: Aggregates leaf nodes within each sub-hub without diluting the effect of an individually severe node.
rows.freq: Every time a sub-hub is recalculated

nosotros.title: Science, engineering, and experience at the service of {accent} diagnosis.

bio: He is a Mechanical Engineer, Specialist in Applied Mathematics (with an emphasis in Operations Research), Specialist in Occupational Risk Management, M.Sc. in Industrial Engineering, M.Sc. Candidate in Materials Engineering, and Ph.D. Candidate in Industry and Organizations. He has more than 15 years of professional experience and 8 years of experience as a university lecturer in engineering and basic sciences.

Throughout his career, he has led engineering, research, and consulting projects for organizations in the oil and gas, energy, infrastructure, construction, manufacturing, transportation, and services sectors, advising more than 100 organizations on comprehensive risk management, industrial safety, occupational hygiene, road safety, fleet management, ergonomics, and integrated management systems.

His scientific work integrates complex systems modeling, network science, systems dynamics, operations research, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, materials engineering, and plasma physics, including research in optical emission spectroscopy (OES) and magnetron sputtering for the development of advanced materials. His work focuses on designing scientific models and evidence-based solutions that make it possible to understand, predict, and optimize complex systems, strengthening decision-making in organizations and institutions.
